conditions.image: release profile, thumbv7em-none-eabihf, no extra features; firmware hash not captured
conditions.links: FerroHAL's F401 links J1 (PA9-PA10) and J2 (PA11-PA12) fitted; PA9 and PA11 driven as GPIO by the firmware
equipment: Nucleo-F401RE (MB1136) through its ST-LINK V2-1, probe 0674FF555185754867115446

measurements.clocks: sysclk 84 MHz, pclk1 42 MHz, pclk2 84 MHz
measurements.sbus_line_health: overruns 0, framing 0, parity 0, noise 0, dma errors 0, dma overruns 0, buffer overruns 0, restarts 0, marks lost 0
measurements.ticks_200ms: TIM4 200 (0 gaps, last 200), TIM3 50 (0 gaps, last 50)
measurements.usart6: 1024 bytes read, 0 wrong, 0 gaps, 71 wakes (63 idle)

observations: Run by an agent on ubuntu-beefcake at the coordinator's board grant, from a fresh clone detached at this revision.

Every member's vector was enabled; both timers ticked at their rates with no gap; every telemetry byte came back once and in order and the reader woke on idle lines; the decoder counted 100 good frames and the one bad chunk, and the firmware's task got 100 updates, the last equal to the last frame sent; the firmware exited through semihosting with success.
The firmware tags the bad-chunk check [PORT-121, PORT-122]; the procedure maps it to PORT-123 as well, which this run's result covers.
limitations: Built and run from revision 2d95702, the commit this record is made at.
Run directly, not through the rig telemetry wrapper, which is not on the rig machine yet; the run is not in the rig log.
The RTT log stayed on the rig PC (hil/logs/f401-rx-ports.log in the runner's clone) and is not attached; the figures above are as the runner reported them.
